predecessors.name: Sultanate of Malacca
predecessors.text: Perak, where Muzaffar Shah, a Malacca prince, was 'invited to rule' after the Malacca sultan's death in 1528

successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Perak, under a British Resident from the Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1877 shape contains all 73 cells of the last Perak shape

ledger.x: 1528: a Malacca prince founds the Sultanate of Perak.
1819: the inland districts of Hulu Perak pass to Reman, a Siamese tributary.
1826: Perak cedes the Dindings and Pangkor to the British.
1826: Siam's pressure on Perak ends with the Burney Treaty.
1874: the Pangkor Treaty puts a British Resident in Perak and redraws the Dindings.
1876: the Perak War ends and the sultanate's independence with it.

wars.name: Acehnese conquest of Perak
wars.outcome: 'In 1620, the Acehnese sultanate invaded Perak and captured its sultan'; after Sultan Sallehuddin died in 1635 'Perak chieftains were left with no alternative but to turn to Aceh's sultan Iskandar Thani', who sent Raja Sulong as Muzaffar Shah II.

wars.name: Kedah's attack on Perak for Siam
wars.outcome: Perak's sultan was set aside after 18 November 1818; Reman, a Siamese tributary, took the inland districts.

wars.name: Larut Wars
wars.outcome: Ended by the Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874, which recognised Abdullah as sultan and brought a British Resident.

wars.name: Perak War
wars.outcome: After Birch's murder in 1875 the British took Pasir Salak on 12 December 1875 and by mid-1876 ended the resistance; Abdullah and Ngah Ibrahim were exiled to the Seychelles and Perak stayed under a British Resident.

certainty.note: No survey line: the Perak River basin and its tin districts, with the Hulu Perak frontier moving with Reman (from 1819) and Aceh's influence.
The Pangkor Treaty fixes the sultan's status, not a surveyed boundary; the Dindings are the only treaty-defined land.
